bug_semantics: Authenticated glossary create/update builds INSERT/UPDATE via sprintf into quoted SQL after $db->escape(). Truncating the already-escaped item with substr(..., 254) can keep a dangling backslash and drop the escaped quote, so the next quote (meant to open definition) closes the item literal and the attacker-controlled definition is parsed as SQL. Users with addglossary or editglossary can extract hashes, salt, and other rows. phpMyFAQ <= 4.1.6, patched in 4.1.7.
flaw_origin: On 2023-09-11 Thorsten Rinne limited glossary items to 254 characters by wrapping the SQL-bound item in substr($item, 0, 254) in Glossary::addGlossaryItem and updateGlossaryItem (8b14f8c1f097480d2013a0f78fb198e008d9bf5a). UPDATE had already done $item = $db->escape($item), so this first wrote escape-then-truncate into the interpolated UPDATE. Parent 0db96193a3529ffc3801b94520f8d924c09bbd6c interpolates htmlspecialchars($item) with no substr. Later 781fdb661 moved the queries into GlossaryRepository and applied the same escape-then-substr order to create(); 48b8b9076 only renamed that into $safeItem. 9d58a7f8c then dropped FILTER_SANITIZE_SPECIAL_CHARS on JSON item/definition, leaving the 4.1.6 HTTP path unsanitized.

CVE.org is PUBLISHED, the vendor GHSA is not withdrawn, and 4.1.6 still has the sink plus unsanitized JSON item/definition. The 4.1.7 patch bb3f06bd27c1291d0d424d5365e465b2b4908b01 (and main twin eb9cafbd) truncates before escaping, which is the patched boundary.
